findings.failureScenario: The CR2 slice tag (CR2_SLICE) values s[1] and s[2] are taken from the file unbounded (only >0 checked) and summed with an unchecked iter().sum(). A crafted CR2 with, e.g., slices [1, 2^63, 2^63+1] makes the sum wrap to width=1 in release, which passes the total%width check. Mode::Full then executes data[y*width+x0 .. +sw] with sw=2^63 and panics (debug builds panic at the sum). Opening the file in the app crashes the decode thread, or aborts the web build (panic=abort). The sibling sRAW path uses try_fold/checked_add (cr2/sraw.rs:87).
findings.action: Sum the widths with checked_add (as sraw.rs does) and reject any slice width greater than the frame's samples per row before slicing.

findings.failureScenario: For lossy DNG (compression 34892), decode_chunk bounds n=cw*ch*cpp by MAX_SAMPLES, but lossy_jpeg() hands the chunk to zune-jpeg with max width/height 65536 and never compares the JPEG's own frame header with the chunk dimensions before decode(). A tiny crafted DNG whose tile is a JPEG header declaring 65535x65535 RGB (with a truncated body, accepted because strict mode is off) makes the decoder allocate about 12.9 GB of output per tile. Tiles are decoded in parallel, so this exhausts memory or aborts on allocation failure. The only size check (line 239) runs after the allocation.
findings.action: Call decode_headers() first and reject a JPEG whose dimensions exceed the chunk's cw x ch (or MAX_SAMPLES), or set max_width/max_height to the chunk dimensions.
